hits.title: One cycle versus two: is logarithmic time necessary in low-memory MPC?
hits.question_text: One cycle versus two: is logarithmic time necessary in low-memory MPC? For every fixed $0<\delta<1$, must every randomized MPC algorithm distinguishing one n-cycle from two vertex-disjoint (n/2)-cycles use $\Omega(\log n)$ rounds in the worst case over even n and input placement? Each machine has $O(n^\delta)$ words and total memory is O(n) words. Require success probability at least $1-n^{-c}$ for each requested fixed $c>0$. An $o(\log n)$-round algorithm for one fixed $\delta<1$ would refute this lower-bound conjecture. O(1)-Round MPC Algorithms for Multi-Dimensional Grid Graph Connectivity, Euclidean MST and DBSCAN

hits.title: How many rounds does triangle detection require in CONGEST?
hits.question_text: How many rounds does triangle detection require in CONGEST? For arbitrary simple undirected n-vertex networks, determine the optimal worst-case randomized round complexity of triangle detection in CONGEST, up to constant factors. Each vertex initially knows its distinct O(log n)-bit identifier and its neighbors, and may send a separate O(log n)-bit message in each direction of every incident edge per synchronous round. On a triangle-free graph all vertices must output NO; otherwise at least one must output YES. The joint answer must be correct with probability at least 2/3 on every input and identifier assignment. The algorithm is uniform, has private random bits, and may know n. The currently established bounds are $\Omega(\log\log n)$ and $\widetilde O(n^{1/3})$. Distributed Subgraph Finding - ADGA 2025

hits.title: Can circle–segment reporting on connected planar graphs have additive output cost?
hits.question_text: Can circle-segment reporting on connected planar graphs have additive output cost? Is there a deterministic static data structure that preprocesses a connected straight-line planar graph with n >= 2 edges in $O(n\log^3 n)$ time and space and reports all k edges intersecting a query circle in $O(\log^3 n+k)$ worst-case time? The graph is embedded in the Euclidean plane: edges are nonzero closed line segments, distinct edge interiors are disjoint, and edges meet only at shared endpoints. A query supplies a center c and radius r > 0. Promise that the circle contains no graph vertex on its boundary and is tangent to no edge. Report each intersected input edge once. All hidden constants are independent of the graph, circle, and output size. Adaptive and Scalable Data Structures (Dagstuhl Seminar 25191)

hits.question_text: Does worst-case Nearest Codeword hardness imply low-noise LPN hardness? Does the following implication hold? If binary Nearest Codeword is not in BPP, then no uniform probabilistic polynomial-time distinguisher D has advantage at least $n^{-c}$, for any fixed $c>0$ and all sufficiently large square n, between $(A,As+e)$ and $(A,u)$. Here $A\in\mathbb F_2^{n^2\times n}$, $s\in\mathbb F_2^n$, and $u\in\mathbb F_2^{n^2}$ are independent uniform random variables, and the coordinates of e are independent Bernoulli variables with rate $1/\sqrt n$. hits.title: Do single-pair shortest paths require cubic-size min-plus circuits?
hits.question_text: Do single-pair shortest paths require cubic-size min-plus circuits? For n >= 2, assign an arbitrary nonnegative real weight x_{ij} to every unordered edge {i,j} of the complete undirected graph on vertices 1,...,n. Define $f_n(x)=\min_{P:1\leadsto n}\sum_{e\in P}x_e$, where P ranges over simple paths. A circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with input gates x_{ij} and optional constants 0 and infinity, binary gates min(a,b) or a+b, unrestricted reuse of gate outputs, and one designated output. Its topology depends on n but not on x, and it must compute f_n exactly for every permitted weight assignment. Let s(n) be the minimum number of binary gates in such a circuit. Is s(n)=Omega(n^3)? Equivalently, do there exist constants c>0 and n0 such that every such circuit has at least c n^3 gates for every n>=n0? Lower Bounds for Tropical Circuits and Dynamic Programs

hits.title: Can exact weighted all-pairs shortest paths be computed in truly subcubic time?
hits.question_text: Can exact weighted all-pairs shortest paths be computed in truly subcubic time? hits.question_text: Can directed reachability be decided in deterministic logarithmic space? Is there a deterministic Turing machine A and an absolute constant C such that, for every directed graph G on vertices {1,...,n} and every s,t, A decides whether t is reachable from s while using at most $C\log_2(n+2)$ work-tape cells? G is supplied explicitly as a read-only adjacency matrix, together with s and t. The machine must halt and be correct on every input. This is equivalent to L=NL. Mathematics and Computation

hits.title: Can reachability diameter be approximated within a constant in near-linear time?
hits.question_text: Can reachability diameter be approximated within a constant in near-linear time? For an unweighted directed graph $G=(V,E)$, define $D(G)=\max\{d_G(u,v):d_G(u,v)<\infty\}$. Is there an absolute constant $C\ge1$ and one randomized word-RAM algorithm that, on every input, returns an estimate $D(G)/C\le\widehat D\le D(G)$ with probability at least 2/3 in $\widetilde O(n+m)$ worst-case time? Here $n=|V|$, $m=|E|$, words have $\Theta(\log n)$ bits, and self-distances are included, giving D(G)=0 on an edgeless graph. The constant and the hidden logarithmic exponent are independent of G. hits.question_text: Can directed reachability have near-linear work and polylogarithmic depth? Given an $n$-vertex, $m$-edge directed graph and a source $s$, is there a randomized shared-memory parallel algorithm that outputs every vertex reachable from $s$ using $\widetilde O(n+m)$ total work and $(\log n)^{O(1)}$ depth, with high probability? Both bounds must hold on arbitrary inputs, including sparse graphs with long directed paths. Work counts all primitive operations across processors; depth is the longest chain of dependent operations. hits.title: Does the expected redundancy of optimal alphabetic trees with random weights converge?
hits.question_text: Does the expected redundancy of optimal alphabetic trees with random weights converge? For each n >= 2, let $D=(D_1,\ldots,D_n)$ be uniform on the probability simplex, equivalently Dirichlet(1,...,1). Let $C_n(D)=\min_T\sum_{i=1}^n D_i d_T(i)$, where T ranges over full ordered binary trees with leaves 1,...,n in that left-to-right order and d_T(i) is the depth of leaf i, with root depth zero. Define $H(D)=-\sum_iD_i\log_2D_i$ and $r_n=\mathbb E_D[C_n(D)-H(D)]$. Does the real sequence r_n converge to a finite limit as n tends to infinity? This is a precise limit-existence target within the source’s broader request to determine the expected optimal cost.
